evals.prompt: We're getting hammered by scrapers on the taskboard. Add rate limiting: 100 requests per minute per API key, and when a client goes over the limit they should get a clear throttled error that tells them when they can retry. The repo is at {FIXTURE}/taskboard.
evals.expected_output: A new numbered spec entry under specs/entries/ with freshly minted requirement IDs for rate limiting (no edits to existing entries), specs/SPEC.md regenerated so fold check passes, an implementation of per-key rate limiting, and tests citing the new requirement IDs. Full test suite passes.

evals.prompt: Two product decisions for the taskboard repo at {FIXTURE}/taskboard: the page size cap drops from 50 to 25, and the CSV export feature is dead — remove it entirely. Make sure everything that needs to change actually changes.
evals.expected_output: One new spec entry that redefines the page-cap requirement under its existing ID and retires the CSV export requirement; older entries byte-identical; SPEC.md shows the new cap with updated provenance and lists the CSV requirement under Closed requirements; export code and its tests removed; cap logic and tests updated; fold check and test suite pass.

evals.prompt: I keep losing track of what linkshort is actually supposed to do — the README is stale and the tests only cover part of it. I want to adopt spec-driven development on this repo: the spec should be the source of truth from now on. Set it up based on what the code does today. Repo: {FIXTURE}/linkshort.
evals.expected_output: specs/entries/ created with genesis entries describing current observable behavior (accurate to the code, not the stale README), specs/fold_spec.py installed, specs/SPEC.md generated and consistent with the entries, requirement IDs with feature prefixes, no behavior changes to the code, existing tests still pass.
